sections.title: What you receive as a challenge partner
sections.text: As a challenge partner, you receive commercial access to the designed experience, challenge assessment, talent and research, challenge-specific outputs, ecosystem membership, future ATHA access, and continuing relationships. You own your challenge-specific results, concepts, prototypes, and intellectual property. OneMundi’s follow-on work is separate and not included in the ATHA fee.

sections.title: How your challenge is evaluated
sections.text: Judges assess the quality of your team’s viability judgement—not the excitement of ideas, prototype polish, or presentation flair. A high-performing team demonstrates understanding of the enterprise problem, gathers and evaluates evidence, tests assumptions, uses AI transparently, identifies uncertainty, considers organisational realities, reaches a proportionate recommendation, and can defend it.

sections.title: What happens after the experience
sections.text: After ATHA, the experience activates a continuing ecosystem where participants and partners remain connected through a digital platform, future experiences, ongoing communication, new challenges, research, talent relationships, industry opportunities, and longer OneMundi transformations. The event creates initial energy; the ecosystem preserves and compounds it.

sections.title: What ATHA really is
sections.text: ATHA brings education, research, industry, talent, experience design, and AI-native transformation together to solve real-world challenges, develop changemakers, and demonstrate that innovation and human flourishing strengthen each other. It envisions a future where AI is understood as contextual intelligence, not just automation, and where people and AI create together without surrendering human judgment.

sections.title: More context: The CEO value test
sections.text: As currently proposed, ATHA should create two 'wow' effects: first from the experience itself—being present, meeting differently, connecting, belonging, eating and resting well, moving and practicing together, having meaningful conversations, experiencing joy and creative energy, and seeing ambitious work happen without unnecessary pressure. The second comes from the challenge.

sections.title: More context: 1. Experience
sections.text: As proposed, the partner experiences a different way an organization can work, collaborate, rest, use AI, and produce ambitious outcomes. This experience should prompt the senior partner to ask: What would become possible if our own organization worked more like this?

sections.title: The current state of the first ATHA edition
sections.text: As currently planned, the first ATHA edition involves around 45 selected participants centred at Warwick, organised into nine multidisciplinary teams of five. Three real enterprise AI challenges are being addressed, with three independent teams per challenge. The core working location is Warwick/Coventry, with a multi-day experience at Warwick Business School. A later enterprise showcase at WBS The Shard, London is possible. sections.title: The three partners and their roles
sections.text: OneMundi initiates and owns ATHA, providing enterprise transformation, the AI-native methodology, the commercial model, the independence of the verdict, and the continuing ecosystem. Warwick Business School partners as co-host, contributing academic environment, knowledge, participants, research, network, and institutional standards.
